domain.purpose: Supply the Git understanding people need to participate effectively in their current activity, without requiring a course or context adapter.
includes: working-tree and editor save versus staging and committing
local versus remote changes and publication
collaboration, pull requests, merge and approvals
evidence, uncertainty and non-destructive recovery explanations
VS Code Source Control interface when relevant
excludes: general AI tutoring unrelated to Git
standalone Git workflow automation or command execution
AIDE stage management, reviews, approvals or artifacts
unrelated business, course or code-review questions

direct: What is the difference between save, stage and commit?
Why did my Git push not show up in the pull request?
implicit: My teammate can't see the change, after I committed it in our repository.
The exercise changed when I switched branches.
followups: So can they see it now? after the learner has been discussing a local commit
And what about approval? after a discussion of a Git pull request
negative: Please review the business requirements for clarity, with no Git context.
Save this email draft, with no repository or Git context.

signals: explicit requests for more or less depth
current activity context when available; no adapter or audience-based proficiency required
